steps.step: 1. A full mesh, exported and run in a solver
steps.evidence: Mesh marched from the wall to 500 chords, written as OpenFOAM polyMesh and SU2. Seven RANS cases run on NACA 0012; see the solver table.

steps.step: 2. Trailing-edge topology from corner element counts
steps.evidence: Sharp and blunt edges through one code path. No irregular node anywhere; along-wall spacing ratio at most 1.17 (the audit measured 36); minimum angle 81–85° where the marched collar had 17–47°.
Camber 0–9% and thickness 6–24% measured, against deformation. Still to do: random CST and UIUC sections, and a comparison against pyHyp itself rather than our own O-mesh.
Not started. The marching already fixes first cell height and orthogonality, so what is left to optimise is the wake-line shape, the along-wall distribution and the dissipation settings.
Not started. This is where the medial radius comes back in, as the cap on layer thickness inside a slot.

defects.where: Far wake, first layers off the wake cut
defects.cause: First cell height on the wake cut stopped growing 2 chords downstream, leaving cells 4 chords long and 0.0002 tall (aspect ratio 20,000).
defects.after: Cell height on the wake cut now grows with the streamwise spacing.

defects.where: Inside the boundary layer over the leading edge
defects.cause: Averaging the along-wall cell size, meant for the far field, also changed the marched height of thin cells wherever wall spacing was graded.
defects.after: Averaging is weighted by cell aspect and leaves thin cells alone.

defects.where: Across the wake line, blunt trailing edge
defects.reported: 35.4° between the C block and the base strip
defects.cause: The first cell on the wake cut and the strip beside it widened at different rates.
defects.after: Both use one widening law. Worst face in the mesh is now 12.9° at the default resolution and 3.7° on the fine mesh.

defects.where: Around the trailing edge at very fine first cells
defects.reported: 45.7° at a first cell of 1e-6 chord
defects.cause: Streamwise spacing at the trailing edge was a fixed number, so the corner cell's aspect ratio rose as the first cell shrank.
defects.after: Trailing-edge spacing is derived from the first cell height (aspect ratio 135).

limits: The outer boundary is wherever the march ends. It is not yet fitted to a supplied far-field curve, and it lands about 20% inside the nominal radius upstream because thick far-field cells fall short of their prescribed height.
The C block is identified as the longest wall segment between wake corners. That is right for one trailing edge and has not been tested on bodies with several reflex corners.
A corner-free body (ellipse, circle) gets the O-mesh; a single annulus around a body with a trailing edge is kept only as a baseline, since it rounds the corner at about 50°.

The blunt base face is not wall-resolved in its own normal direction: the first cell off the base is one trailing-edge spacing long, and y⁺ there reaches 25 while the rest of the wall averages below 2. The strip needs clustering towards the base.
The solver check is incompressible and uses one turbulence model on one section. Pressure and skin-friction distributions have not been compared, only forces.
The wake line leaves along the trailing-edge bisector and turns onto the x axis over one chord. The mesher is not told the angle of attack.
First cell height is within 0.3% of the request on 12%-thick sections and within 1.1% on the 24%-thick one, at the trailing-edge corner node.
The earlier medial-axis blocking, the interpolated collar and the marched collar are untouched and are not used by this path.
files: src/aeromesh/mesh/: spacing.py (graded node distributions, first cell from y⁺), hyperbolic.py (the marcher), airfoil.py (o_mesh, c_mesh), structured.py (blocks and exact assembly checks), export.py (OpenFOAM, SU2, VTK).
src/aeromesh/quality/metrics.py: wall, boundary-layer and whole-mesh metrics, including the finite-volume non-orthogonality that matches checkMesh.

python validation/camber_sweep.py <work_dir> re-runs the sweep; run_naca0012.py then collect_naca0012.py re-run the solver cases (OpenFOAM 11 needed); make_report.py rebuilds this page from the results.
